summary:
The patient's medical history begins well before the incident at issue: in September 2022, a gym weightlifting accident during a heavy squat set produced severe neck pain and stiffness, evaluated by Dr. Alistair Finch at Back & Spine Restoration Center. That workup culminated in a September 22, 2022 cervical spine X-ray showing mild degenerative disc disease at C5-C6 with a 4mm posterior disc bulge, and a diagnosis of acute cervical strain with possible disc herniation. This finding matters because it resurfaces repeatedly later in the record as a pre-existing condition.

The current claim arises from a motor vehicle accident that left the patient with fractures of the left humerus and radius. On September 4, 2023, Dr. Elizabeth Foster performed emergency open reduction and internal fixation at Littel Inc Emergency Hospital, using a nerve block for anesthesia. A head CT followed on September 5, and fluoroscopic imaging on September 7 confirmed hardware placement and alignment. Acetaminophen 975mg was used for inpatient pain control. Notably, Dr. Foster's own records flagged the C5-C6 disc narrowing and bulge as being of unclear onset, "possibly preexisting" — a characterization Dr. Myrtle Turner later confirmed, tying it back to imaging predating the September 2023 crash.

Rehabilitation began September 15, 2023, with Robert Stewart, PT, DPT at Lang-Weimann Medical Center, addressing the left humerus/radius ORIF, cervicalgia, and a left knee contusion. Progress was steady but complicated by persistent cervical symptom provocation during traction and mobilization work. Dr. Turner's October 19 follow-up showed early callus formation but significant neck stiffness and weak grip strength, prompting cyclobenzaprine 10mg; by November 16, worsening arm and neck pain led to high-dose ibuprofen 800mg. The patient then missed three consecutive PT sessions in mid-November, and by November 24 had suffered a significant rebound in elbow stiffness, requiring intensified passive stretching to recover lost ground.

The patient completed 30 sessions at Lang-Weimann by December 11, still with severe cervical stiffness and arm pain, prompting Dr. Turner to order MRI of the left upper extremity and C-spine. December 14 X-rays showed well-healed fractures with stable hardware, though decreased radial sensation and ROM restriction persisted. Care transitioned to Amanda Gregory, PT, OCS at Emory Sports Medicine Complex beginning January 8, 2024, for continued strengthening, cervical traction, and myofascial work — sessions repeatedly interrupted by provoked cervical symptoms through February and March. By March 25, 2024, after a second full course of 30 sessions, the patient had made substantial gains but was left with a persistent 22-degree extension deficit in the left elbow and chronic pain, marking the current, unresolved status.
